title: HateXplain domain-aware prior correction and fit-only threshold
question: M1.40 的 global target_prior 在 HateXplain 上伤害 accuracy；HateXplain 的 Gab/Twitter 两个来源的 hate 先验差异很大。把先验按域拆开后，global prior 的伤害是否消失，且 fit-only 阈值能否保留修正收益？

dataset.name: HateXplain

label_mapping.note: offensive→0 is retained from M1.40; three-class is not part of M1.41.

dataset.note: test labels are used only for evaluation; thresholds never use test labels. Domain labels are metadata, not model inputs.

modeling.c_selection: f32 only, 5-fold StratifiedKFold on fit, accuracy; f32 and quantized arm share C

domain_test_prior.threshold: for each source g: quantile(test scores in g, 1 - prior_fit_g)

domain_fit_prior.threshold: for each source g: quantile(out-of-fold fit scores in g, 1 - prior_fit_g)
domain_fit_prior.note: deployable domain-aware rule; OOF scores come from the same 5 folds used for C selection

H1_domain_misspecification.statement: Because fit Gab hate rate is 0.502 vs Twitter 0.078, one global prior threshold over-predicts Twitter and under-predicts Gab; global_test_prior accuracy is below default overall, with the largest loss on Twitter.

H2_domain_correction.statement: domain_test_prior improves overall accuracy over global_test_prior, and improves Twitter accuracy over global_test_prior; Gab is expected to improve or stay neutral.

H3_inductive_threshold.statement: domain_fit_prior retains most of the domain_test_prior gain without using any test scores; if it does, the correction is deployable. If it loses the gain, the M1.40 target_prior effect was transductive.

H4_candidate_effect.statement: Under domain-aware thresholds, the quantized arm minus f32 may change sign relative to M1.40, but this is exploratory and cannot upgrade R12/rescan.

primary_endpoint.units: depth x probe x seed; 2 depths x 2 probes x 5 seeds = 20 cells; quantized arms are secondary
primary_endpoint.bootstrap: 10,000 paired stratified bootstrap, resample n_gab and n_twitter within each domain, 95% percentile CI

verdict.supported: for each depth/probe family, >=4/5 positive CIs and 5-seed mean > 0
verdict.partially_supported: one probe family meets supported, the other has >=2/5 positive CIs
verdict.rejected: both probe families have <=1/5 positive CIs

primary_endpoint.note: 4 primary families (l12/logreg, l12/linear_svc, l6/logreg, l6/linear_svc); no candidate confirmation.

secondary_endpoints: per-domain accuracy for all rules (gab, twitter)
domain_test_prior - default overall and per domain
domain_fit_prior - domain_test_prior overall and per domain
quantized arm - f32 under domain_test_prior and domain_fit_prior, per domain and overall (exploratory)
predicted positive rate and threshold by rule/domain

independence_and_boundaries.seeds: 5 seeds share the same test texts and often the same C; they are not independent repeats.
independence_and_boundaries.effective_units: domain x C x probe; report seed-level CIs but do not treat 5 seeds as 5 independent studies.
independence_and_boundaries.corpus: single official HateXplain test, n=1,918; domain split is internal, not a third corpus.
independence_and_boundaries.labels: offensive→0 is an external mapping boundary; three-class is not tested here.
independence_and_boundaries.candidate: R12 and rescan were rejected in M1.40; M1.41 is a calibration/mechanism experiment, not a candidate rescue.
independence_and_boundaries.test_scores: global_test_prior and domain_test_prior use unlabeled test scores (transductive); domain_fit_prior is the deployable control.

prereg_commit_policy: This file is committed before running any model-score or accuracy computation. Data-source counts and hashes above are audit metadata only.
